title: IFrames
definition: The `<iframe>` (Inline Frame) element represents a nested browsing context, embedding another HTML page into the current one.
simpleExplanation: A window cut into your website that looks out at another website. The website inside the iframe functions completely independently of your main website.
realWorldExample: Embedding a YouTube video or a Google Map. YouTube doesn't give you the MP4 file; they give you an `<iframe>` code that loads their custom video player webpage in a small box on your site.

basic: What attribute is used to tell the iframe what website to display?
intermediate: Can you use JavaScript on your main site to click buttons inside an iframe from another domain?

answers.question: Cross-domain JavaScript control?
answers.answer: No. This is blocked by the Same-Origin Policy for security. If you embed `bank.com` in an iframe, your JavaScript cannot reach inside the iframe and click 'Transfer Funds'. The browser strictly separates them.
